mission.display_title: Evaluate probabilities and quantiles for placed families
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to turn Beta's family placement into probability and quantile evaluation. So you can compute or obtain P and quantile answers for the univariate families you already recognise, without pretending Poisson-process or generation LOs are finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to evaluate probabilities and quantiles for named univariate families using calculation or software as appropriate. And to refuse treating family recognition alone as evaluation skill.

mission.learning_objective: Evaluate probabilities and quantiles associated with the basic univariate distributions already placed (by calculation or using statistical software as appropriate).
mission.concept_focus: Named family → probability or quantile question → method (tables/software/calculation) → refuse recognition-as-evaluation theatre.
mission.prior_bridge: Campaign Beta ended after continuous family placement (2.1.2) and Revision. Today continues topic 2.1 at LO 2.1.3 (evaluation) not a new chapter leap.

mission.expected_benefit: Study Progress for probability/quantile evaluation. Not Topic Complete for 2.1.4–2.1.6.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Gamma Day 1 because CE-001 / EP-001 Continuity Front names 2.1.3 as the handoff from Beta.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: probability vs quantile
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For a named continuous family, which statement correctly distinguishes a probability question, a quantile question, and an acceptable method class?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Evaluation skill starts by discriminating the question type and naming a method class.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: State a P-question, a quantile question, and a method class such as calculation, tables, or software.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Restating the family name without posing an evaluation question.

choices.label: Probability: find P(X <= 2) for X ~ Exp(lambda). Quantile: find x such that P(X <= x) = 0.95. Method class: calculation, tables, or software CDF/quantile functions as appropriate.
Naming the family is already both the probability and the quantile evaluation, so no method class is required.
A quantile question asks for P(X <= a), while a probability question asks for the x with given cumulative probability.
Only software menus count as a method class; hand calculation and tables are never acceptable for continuous families.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: Exponential CDF probability
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Travel medical claim sizes X (£) are modelled as Exponential with mean θ = 250. Compute P(X ≤ 100). Enter the probability as a decimal.
knowledge_checks.body: Evaluate the Exponential CDF at the stated threshold.
hints: Use F(x) = 1 - e^{-x/θ} with θ = 250 and x = 100.
Report a decimal probability, not a percentage.
knowledge_checks.explanation: For Exponential mean θ, P(X ≤ x) = 1 - e^{-x/θ}. Here x/θ = 100/250 = 0.4, so P(X ≤ 100) = 1 - e^{-0.4} ≈ 0.3297. Naming the Exponential family alone does not produce this probability.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Reporting e^{-0.4} ≈ 0.6703 (the survival probability) instead of 1 - e^{-0.4}, or treating θ = 250 as a rate so that F(100) = 1 - e^{-25000}.
success_criteria: Uses the Exponential CDF with mean θ, not the survival function alone.

worked_example.title: Exponential severity probability and median
worked_example.problem_statement: Travel medical claim sizes X (£) are modelled as Exponential with mean θ = 250. Compute (a) P(X ≤ 100) and (b) the median claim size.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Use the Exponential CDF F(x) = 1 - e^{-x/θ} and the median formula θ ln 2.

steps.label: Evaluate P(X ≤ 100)
steps.explanation: For Exponential mean θ, P(X ≤ x) = 1 - e^{-x/θ}. Here x/θ = 100/250 = 0.4.

steps.label: Evaluate the median
steps.explanation: The median m satisfies 1 - e^{-m/θ} = 0.5, so m = θ ln 2.

steps.label: Refuse recognition-as-evaluation
steps.attempt_cue: State why naming 'Exponential' alone is not the evaluation.
steps.explanation: Recognising the family is not the same as evaluating the probability and quantile. The LO requires the numeric CDF and median results.

worked_example.final_answer: P(X ≤ 100) ≈ 0.3297; median ≈ 173.29. Naming the Exponential family alone does not finish the evaluation.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Stopping after recognising that the size is Exponential, without computing the CDF probability and the median quantile.
